html:
The Guatemalan Civil War was fought from 1960 to 1996 between the government and left-wing guerrillas. About 200,000 people were killed or disappeared, most of them Maya civilians killed by the state.

It began with a revolt of junior officers and grew into guerrilla war after the coup of 1954 closed peaceful roads to reform. Military governments, backed by the United States, fought the rebels with death squads in the cities. Around 1981 to 1983, under Ríos Montt and his predecessor, the army destroyed hundreds of Maya villages in the highlands, and over a million people fled.

A UN-backed truth commission in 1999 found that the state had committed genocide against Maya groups. The Esquipulas process led to peace in 1996. The Guatemalan civil war page covers the war in more depth. Rigoberta Menchú told its story to the world.
sum: The Guatemalan Civil War was fought from 1960 to 1996 between the government and left-wing guerrillas. About 200,000 people were killed or disappeared, most of them Maya civilians killed by the state.
